Quote source · Q0055

Who said “Once in a lifetime, everything must be doubted”?

The located source for this passage, the original-language wording where one exists, and the forms of it that circulate without the attribution.

Quote source / René Descartes / Once in a lifetime, everything…

English

Once in a lifetime, everything must be doubted.
Thinker René Descartes
Work Meditations on First Philosophy I
School Rationalism
Theme Doubt

Checked against the cited edition on 2026-09-14.

The recorded source

Attributed to
René Descartes
Work and locator
Meditations on First Philosophy I
English wording
“Once in a lifetime, everything must be doubted.”
Original wording (Latin)
Semel in vita de omnibus, quantum fieri potest, esse dubitandum.

“Once in a life, as far as possible, everything must be doubted.” The words “once in a lifetime” carry the whole method: this is a single act of demolition, not a standing policy.

Exact wording and the variants in circulation

A quotation in English from a non-English source has two versions, and they are not interchangeable.

No divergent wording is recorded for this passage: the English in circulation matches the wording cited above.

Attribution notes

The sentence is Descartes' statement of the method of the first Meditation. It is routinely recited as a general endorsement of scepticism, which inverts it: Descartes doubts once in order to find something that cannot be doubted, and the point of the exercise is the foundation he reaches at the end of the second Meditation.
